Resolves: #560314

Prior to __strictDeps Git's own setup/build would provide a variant of libintl.h that would propagate itself to $out. That unintentional side effect disappeared after and the internationalization support it provided dropped with it. This change ships it explicitly when nlsSupport evals to true.

items.content_html:
Add fzf-git-sh-unwrapped, which installs upstream's Bash/Zsh and Fish plugins unchanged so runtime commands such as fzf and bat are resolved from PATH.

Refactor the existing fzf-git-sh package to derive from the unwrapped package while retaining its absolute store substitutions, output layout, and runtime closure. The wrapped package also exposes passthru.unwrapped.

This addresses the sourcing concern raised in #521555:

  • Bash and Zsh checks source the installed plugin, verify its self-resolved path, and re-enter the installed script.
  • The Fish check resolves the sibling fzf-git.sh path, delegates through Bash, and exercises --run list_bindings.
  • PATH-only test doubles exercise fzf and bat resolution.
  • The unwrapped output has no references to nixpkgs fzf or bat and the existing wrapped output retains both.

Automation disclosure: Codex (GPT-5) assisted with implementation, testing, and drafting this PR. I reviewed and edited myself

items.content_html:
Description of changes

This makes it possible to include git commit and tag signature verification when using fetchgit.

The motivation for this is to enable maintainers to ensure an update to the source code was authorized by the developers.
As signing keys are supposed to stay the same over multiple versions, they should remain unchanged when updating to a new revision of a given source code.

The verification is done in a non-fixed-output derivation so it will always be executed.
See https://landweber.xyz/ba.pdf Section 5.1.5 and #43233 (comment).

The pr mimics the behaviior of the verified-fetches experimental feature introduced by NixOS/nix#8848.

items.content_html:
Fixes #566500.

The bup 0.34 update (#565549) changed how bup parses --remote: it now accepts only [user@]host:[path] or an ssh:///bup:// URL. git-annex's bup special remote passes every buprepo= via -r, so initremote, copy and get fail with remote PATH has no colon for a bup remote whose buprepo is a local path. That's the bup remote failure Hydra shows on master for both x86_64-linux (https://hydra.nixos.org/build/346774193) and aarch64-darwin (https://hydra.nixos.org/build/346774093), but it isn't only the check phase: those remotes are broken at runtime too, so skipping the test would just hide it.

This adds a small patch to Remote/Bup.hs that passes local-path repositories with bup's global --bup-dir (-d) option instead, which is long-standing and present in bup 0.33 as well. The empty buprepo (bup's default repository) and host:path remotes still go through -r exactly as before. Upstream hasn't fixed this: bupParams is unchanged in 10.20260901 and in git-annex master as of 7c2e8019c98c, and it hasn't been reported there yet.

I'm targeting master because the breakage arrived with the bup bump on master, and the rebuild is small (git-annex and the handful of packages that depend on it, mostly the datalad family). haskell-updates (git-annex 10.20260901, also with bup 0.34) needs this too: the patch applies there unchanged (offset 2), but haskell-updates adds git-annex-crypton-1.1.patch at the same spot in the patches list, so the next master merge into haskell-updates should keep both entries. I'm happy to open the haskell-updates side as well if that's preferred.

I used Claude Code (claude-opus-5-5) to diagnose the failure, write the patch, run the builds and tests below, and draft this description. I've reviewed the change and the results, and the commit carries an Assisted-by: trailer.

Things done

  • Built on platform:
    • x86_64-linux
    • aarch64-linux
    • aarch64-darwin
  • Tested, as applicable:
    • NixOS tests in nixos/tests.
    • Package tests at passthru.tests.
    • Tests in lib/tests or pkgs/test for functions and "core" functionality.
  • Ran nixpkgs-review on this PR. See nixpkgs-review usage.
  • Tested basic functionality of all binary files, usually in ./result/bin/. The check phase passes on both platforms with bup remote OK in every repository mode (darwin keeps nixpkgs' usual -p '!/addurl/'). In a smoke test on aarch64-darwin with the built git-annex and bup 0.34, a remote with buprepo=/abs/path handles initremote, copy --to, drop, get --from and fsck --from, which covers every bup call git-annex makes (init, split, join).

Smoke test

With git-annex, bup, git and coreutils from this branch on PATH:

set -euxo pipefail
work=$(mktemp -d)
export HOME=$work/home GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1
mkdir -p "$HOME"
git config --global user.name smoke
git config --global user.email smoke@example.invalid
git config --global init.defaultBranch main
cd "$work"
git init -q repo
cd repo
git annex init smoke
echo hello > file

items.content_html:
llvmPackages_22.compiler-rt-no-libc does not build on aarch64-linux, which takes llvmPackages_22.libcxx, libcxxClang and clangUseLLVM down with it (same for llvmPackages_23 and llvmPackages_git). Hydra has no aarch64-linux build of any of those jobs, while the llvmPackages_21 ones build.

Cause: llvm/llvm-project#161751 (in 22.1.0 and later) removed the __has_include(<sys/auxv.h>) guards from the AArch64 LSE-atomics and FMV feature detection in compiler-rt/lib/builtins/cpu_model/aarch64.c. The no-libc variant has no libc headers, so the file fails with

compiler-rt/lib/builtins/cpu_model/aarch64.c:51:10: fatal error: 'sys/auxv.h' file not found

Fix: in the existing !haveLibc block of compiler-rt/default.nix, restore the guards with a substituteInPlace, gated on Linux, aarch64 and LLVM >= 22. (The Linux part matters: Darwin builds compiler-rt-no-libc without a libc as well, and without it every llvmPackages_{22,23} derivation on aarch64-darwin would rebuild for no effect, which is what the first eval of this PR showed.) That gives the LLVM 21 behaviour back: LSE detection is skipped and __aarch64_have_lse_atomics stays false when there is no libc. The FMV branch is already compiled out in this configuration by COMPILER_RT_DISABLE_AARCH64_FMV (ded560c, same block, same gate). The substituted line is identical in 22.1.8, 23.1.0 and the git snapshot (two occurrences each), so --replace-fail covers all three.

Only compiler-rt-no-libc and what is built on top of it change, and only on aarch64-linux. Checked with nix-instantiate against master for LLVM 21, 22, 23 and git: compiler-rt-libc, clang, libllvm, lld and the stdenv keep their derivations; nothing changes on x86_64-linux or on aarch64-darwin.

Fixes #495155. Upstream context: llvm/llvm-project#127227 (acyclic compiler-rt/libc bootstrap) and llvm/llvm-project#152394 (proposed no-libc-headers build mode, still open); until something like that lands, restoring the LLVM 21 guard is the smallest change that keeps the no-libc build working.

Context: this came out of packaging redpanda-server, which is built with llvmPackages_22.libcxxClang; with this fix it builds and passes its NixOS test natively on aarch64-linux.

Things done

  • Built on platform:
    • x86_64-linux (no derivation changes; nixpkgs-review reports nothing to rebuild)
    • aarch64-linux (Raspberry Pi 5): llvmPackages_22.compiler-rt-no-libc, llvmPackages_22.libcxx, llvmPackages_23.compiler-rt-no-libc, llvmPackages_23.libcxx build; without the change llvmPackages_23.compiler-rt-no-libc fails with the error above. A full application (redpanda-server, libc++ 22, ~8,600 Bazel actions) builds against the result and passes its NixOS VM test.
    • aarch64-darwin (not affected: the change is gated on isLinux; eval shows no darwin rebuilds)
  • Tested, as applicable:
    • NixOS tests in nixos/tests: nixosTests.redpanda-server (from the companion PR) on aarch64-linux against a libc++ 22 built with this change.
    • Package tests at passthru.tests.
    • Tests in lib/tests or pkgs/test for functions and "core" functionality.
  • Ran nixpkgs-review on this PR. See nixpkgs-review usage. (x86_64-linux: nothing to rebuild.)
